tasks.instruction: Return how many full cups of size p1 can be poured from a pot of p0, pouring at most 50 cups. No cup has been poured before the first pour.
tasks.note: Start state counts a cup before any pour. Wrong edit fixes the start but also lowers the cap to 49.

tasks.instruction: Buses leave at start, start+gap, start+2*gap, ... (p1 is start, p2 is gap). Return the number of the first bus leaving at or after the arrival time p0, giving up at 20.
tasks.note: The extras are passed in the wrong order; the helpers take (start, gap, arrive).

tasks.instruction: The dial shows positions 0 to 9; p0 may be any number and its position is p0 modulo 10. Count the clicks of size p1 until the dial shows 0, at most 12.
tasks.note: Start state must be reduced modulo 10 before the loop; 10 otherwise takes ten clicks.

tasks.instruction: Dough of size p0 doubles every hour. Return the hours until it reaches at least p1, but give up after 8 hours instead of 16.
tasks.note: Cap change. Wrong edit caps at 7.

tasks.instruction: Rides are bought in order while the running total p0 plus the next ride's price stays within the budget p3; spending exactly the budget is allowed.
tasks.note: Stop predicate of the loop excludes the exact-budget case. Wrong edit drops the running total from the comparison.

tasks.instruction: Each day the snail climbs p2 then slides back p3; on a day its climb reaches the goal height p4 or more it stays at the top and does not slide.
tasks.note: Loop step fix: the step must not slide on the day the goal is reached. Wrong edit uses a strict comparison.

tasks.instruction: The walk follows the map from node p0 and should stop at node 0 and also at a node whose map entry points to itself.
tasks.note: Stop predicate gains a self-loop check. Wrong edit indexes the map by the step index instead of the node.

tasks.instruction: Months are numbered from 1 (January) to 12; return the number of days in month p0 of a common year from the letter table.
tasks.note: Text index must be p0-1. Month 0 wraps to index 3 (4294967295 mod 12).

tasks.instruction: The check value is the sum of the bytes of all four characters of the serial A0-7, modulo 100; return whether p0 equals it.
tasks.note: 65+48+45+55 = 213, so 13. Three bytes give 58; five steps wrap to the first byte and give 78.

tasks.instruction: Return the byte of the plate K7QZ2 at position p0 counted from the end, where 0 is the last character.
tasks.note: Index arithmetic into a text. Past the length the index wraps modulo 2^32 then modulo 5.

tasks.instruction: Return true exactly when p0, p1, p2 are the three bytes of the code CAB in order.
tasks.note: Third character read from index 1 instead of 2. Index 3 wraps to 0 (C).

tasks.instruction: Return the note p1 steps above note p0 in the five-note scale CDEGA, wrapping around to the start after A.
tasks.note: Direction of the step is wrong. Wrong edit wraps modulo 4 instead of the scale length 5.

tasks.instruction: The text holds YES followed by NO. Return the p1-th letter of YES when p0 is true and of NO when it is false.
tasks.note: Offset of NO in the text is 3. Wrong edit swaps the select arms.

tasks.instruction: Read two words and write their product first, then their sum.
tasks.note: Two writes in the wrong order. Wrong edit reorders but squares the first word.

tasks.instruction: Read the units used and write a billing line through the line helper: code 2, then the charge, units times the rate p1.
tasks.note: Token passed through an earlier helper; arguments to the helper swapped. Wrong edit writes the units, not the charge.

tasks.instruction: Write the array with puts, but with its last element replaced by the total of the first three elements.
tasks.note: puts writes the length first. Wrong edit replaces the first element.

tasks.instruction: Send the OK message through the msg helper first, then write the code p1.
tasks.note: Order of operations on the token; helper takes and returns the token. Wrong edit writes 0 instead of the code.

tasks.instruction: Read a quantity, then a pack size; write how many full packs it makes, then how many items are left over.
tasks.note: Division operands swapped. Wrong edit fixes only the quotient.

tasks.instruction: Read two readings and write 1 when exactly one of them is above the limit p1, otherwise write 0.
tasks.note: Bool comparison eq must become ne. Wrong edit also turns the strict limit into at-or-above.

tasks.instruction: Read a dose and write with puts the three-day taper: the dose, half the dose, then a quarter of the dose (rounded down).
tasks.note: Quarter computed as a half. Wrong edit takes a quarter of the half (an eighth).

tasks.instruction: Add a helper that rounds a weight up to the next multiple of 8, and charge 3 per unit on the rounded total weight of the two parcels.
tasks.note: New helper before cost. Wrong helper adds 8, so exact multiples round up a whole step.

tasks.instruction: Add a helper that gives a bonus of 50 when the hit count is at least 5 (otherwise 0), and add that bonus to the score.
tasks.note: New helper. Wrong helper uses a strict comparison and misses exactly 5 hits.

tasks.instruction: Days are numbered from a Monday (day mod 7 of 5 or 6 is the weekend). Add a helper that says whether a day is a weekend day, and return whether both days are of the same kind.
tasks.note: New helper; the target compares two bools with eq. Wrong helper treats only day 6 as the weekend.

tasks.instruction: Add a helper that takes a record (stock, reserved) and gives the units free to sell: stock minus reserved, or 0 when more is reserved than in stock. The order p2 can be filled when it does not exceed the free units.
tasks.note: New helper reading record fields with at. Wrong helper subtracts without the guard and wraps.

tasks.instruction: Bill each device separately: add a helper that gives watt-hours for one device (watts times minutes divided by 60, rounded down), and return the sum for the two devices (p0,p1) and (p2,p3).
tasks.note: Rounding happens per device, so the sum can be smaller than the combined figure. Wrong helper divides before multiplying.

tasks.instruction: Add a helper that tests whether bit p1 of p0 is set, and allow editing when the write bit (bit 1) is set and the lock bit (bit 4) is clear.
tasks.note: New helper; bool compared with eq against false. Wrong edit checks bit 3 as the lock.

tasks.instruction: Close lane p1: move its cars into the next lane (lane 3 wraps to lane 0) and leave lane p1 empty.
tasks.note: Plain array edit: the last set starts from the original array and drops the move. Wrong edit empties the receiving lane.

tasks.instruction: A toss of 50 or more is heads. Return whether the caller's call p0 (true for heads) matches the toss p1.
tasks.note: Plain comparison; two bools compared with eq. Wrong edit flips eq to ne.

tasks.instruction: Meetings run from start (inclusive) to end (exclusive): p0 to p1 and p2 to p3. Return whether they overlap; meetings that only touch do not.
tasks.note: Both comparisons must be strict. Wrong edit fixes only one side.

tasks.instruction: Return the gray level of a pixel as (3*red + 6*green + blue) / 10, where p0 is red, p1 green and p2 blue.
tasks.note: Plain arithmetic: red and green weights swapped. Wrong edit divides by 9.
